title: Reduce batch allocator bloat and introduce KV-heartbeat coordinator
creator: Ava Nguyen
description: Problem summary: The continuous batching allocator has been observed to retain oversized slab allocations under long-lived sessions, producing 15–30% higher RSS on model-serving hosts during mixed workloads. Simultaneously, the KV cache uses opportunistic per-shard heartbeats which currently trigger immediate shard reclaims under transient preemption, causing KV churn and increased RPCs to backing store. The scheduler's lease boundary logic can preempt long-running batches when a small priority preemption arrives, amplifying tail latency spikes. This ticket refactors three tightly-coupled paths: shrink the allocation size-classes and introduce a compacting freelist for batch slots; implement a KV-heartbeat coordinator that batches heartbeat/lease renewals and exposes a single heartbeat metric per shard; and simplify lease boundary semantics with an epoch-advance handoff to avoid preempting in-flight mini-batches. Goals: reduce RSS by 15–25% on p99 load, lower KV background RPCs by >40%, and reduce 95/99 tail latency spike incidence under contention.
comments: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after incident postmortem (INC-2026-03-07) showed allocator growth + KV churn as root contributors.
2026-03-11: Spike repro locally with mixed chat+completion workload; profiling shows 27% of heap held in batch-slot slabs; allocator fragmentation correlated with session churn.

2026-03-12: Design review with runtime team. Decision: introduce compacting freelist that runs opportunistically during low CPU periods, not synchronously on free. Also add a small per-tenant ceiling to avoid unbounded growth.
2026-03-12: PM (Priya Shah) requested canary rollout plan and opt-in feature flag for Dedicated customers; noted compliance teams will need release notes for Private installs.

2026-03-13: Diego implemented initial KV-heartbeat coordinator prototype (see PR #1724). It aggregates renewals per-shard on 50ms window and emits a heartbeat metric 'kv.coordinator.heartbeat_ms'. Local unit tests passed.

2026-03-13: Engineering review (Liam O'Connor): asked for clearer invariants around epoch-advance: must guarantee at-most-once release of slot ownership. Diego proposed using 'handoff token' that is single-writer; follow-up PR will add formal assertions and a stress test harness.

2026-03-14: Load test on canary pool (3 hosts) shows 18% RSS reduction and 33% fewer background KV RPCs; observed two p99 latency regressions tied to GC cycles—mitigation: tune freelist compaction backoff and spread work via cooperative yield points.
2026-03-14: Next: harden coordinator to handle shard leader failover and add dashboard panels for kv.heartbeat, batch.slot_utilization, lease.handoff_latency.
acceptance_criteria: Batch allocator compaction implemented behind a feature flag; default enabled in canary; unit and integration tests included.
KV-heartbeat coordinator aggregates renewals and reduces per-shard RPCs by >=40% in canary load tests.
Scheduler epoch-advance handoff prevents preemption of in-flight mini-batches; documented invariant with tests proving at-most-once handoff.
No regression in single-request 95th latency beyond 5% compared to baseline; memory RSS reduction >=15% on mixed workload.
Dashboards added and alerted: kv.coordinator.heartbeat_latency, batch.slot_compaction_time, lease.handoff_failures; runbook updated.
Canary rollout completed across Dedicated pool with rollback plan validated.
Code reviewed by two engineers and approved by runtime lead.
steps: Phase 1 (prototype): implement compacting freelist + KV-heartbeat coordinator. Feature flags: batcher.compaction_opt_in, kv.coordinator_enabled.
Phase 2 (tests): add stress harness for epoch handoff and leader failover, run soak for 48 hours on canary pool.
Phase 3 (observability): add Prometheus metrics, Grafana panels and a Kibana query for lease handoff errors.
Phase 4 (canary rollout): enable flags on 5% traffic, monitor for 72 hours, iterate tuning parameters (compaction window, heartbeat batch window).
Phase 5 (rollout): roll to 25% then 100% for hosted; coordinate Dedicated customer communication and Private release notes.
artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Batcher+Compaction+Design - design doc with benchmarks and trade-offs
risks_mitigation: Risk: aggressive compaction can add latency during collection. Mitigation: adaptive backoff and cooperative yields; default conservative settings in 1.23.
Risk: single coordinator becomes a hotpath. Mitigation: implement sharded coordinator per-NUMA node and fallback to per-shard lease if coordinator fails.
Risk: rollback complexity. Mitigation: all changes behind feature flags; migration is stateless for rollback (compaction idempotent).
qa_plan: Unit tests for allocator invariants and freelist correctness.
Stress test harness that injects preemptions, leader failover, and session churn; run 48h on canary pool.
Regression perf-suite comparing baseline vs feature-on for p50/p95/p99 and RSS memory profile.
Smoke runbook to validate rollback procedure and verify no orphaned slots after rollback.
